title: Through DeFi Saver's eyes
subheading: a stop-motion in graphite. 12 frames a second
content_note: Narrative and financial numbers are observed reference artwork, not financial advice or current product specifications.

captions.text: A short film about what a DeFi loan looks like from my side.
When you connect a wallet, I don't see a face. I see what it owns and what it owes.
Out of all these numbers, I watch one: how far you are from liquidation.
At 3 a.m., the price starts to drop. It doesn't wait for you to wake up.
You drew a line earlier. When the ratio touches it, I sell just enough ETH to pay back part of the loan. All in one transaction.
In the morning the loan is a bit smaller, and it's still yours.
Other days I have other jobs. Moving a loan to another protocol. Fitting five steps into one transaction. Trailing a stop behind a perp. Letting you practice with pretend money first.
I work with 16 protocols on 5 networks. I didn't build any of them. I just know their rules very well.
I never hold your money. I can only do what you signed off on. And I can't stop a crash. I can only react the way you told me to.
Been doing this since 2019. Mostly at night.
